invariant_definitions.write_exact: per world: HYPOTHESIS_PROPOSED == steps+1 (idempotent duplicate yields exactly one), PREDICTION/OBSERVATION/FAILURE/ARTIFACT counts == client-side counts
invariant_definitions.budget_exact: engine consumed == researcher spend == EXPERIMENT_COMMITTED count; BUDGET_EXHAUSTED iff attempted > B
invariant_definitions.index_contiguous/seq_increasing/global_s: ledger index 0..n-1 without gaps per world; event_seq strictly increasing; global seq unique across worlds
invariant_definitions.chain_recompute_ok: independent recomputation of the hash chain over (world_id, world_index, event_type, ts, actor, payload, refs, causal, artifacts, prev_hash, schema_ver=1) from raw sqlite rows
invariant_definitions.f10_deterministic: two F10 calls on the same world/cutoff byte-identical
invariant_definitions.idempotency: two clients, same Idempotency-Key + same body concurrently -> identical response; same key different body -> 409
invariant_definitions.fork_boundary: child F10 == parent F10 at checkpoint seq, for a fork taken under load

per_worker_workload: register, create+start world (enforceable experiments budget B=8), concurrent idempotent duplicate + conflict, 3 LT steps, checkpoint+fork, finish (exceed budget), artifacts, resources, F10 x2, child-vs-parent F10, imports

C1_qualified_operating_envelope.ecology_may_run_at: <=16 concurrent lineages on a pinned instance (and only after ED-001 is resolved)

ENGINE_PERFORMANCE_LIMIT.shape: throughput saturates at ~600 ev/s from L=128 (562/621/609/586); p50 latency grows ~linearly with L (2.0s@256, 4.6s@512, 9.9s@1024) = queueing on the single serialized writer; max latency 31.9s@1024 exceeds sfclient's default timeout (30.0s, sfclient/client.py:40) -> a stock client begins timing out at 1024 while the engine stays correct
ENGINE_PERFORMANCE_LIMIT.classification: ENGINE_PERFORMANCE_LIMIT (latency/queueing), NOT a correctness collapse; no level produced a wrong ledger, wrong budget, wrong F10 or wrong fork frontier

instrument_caveats: sfclient opens one TCP connection per request; at L=256 the FIRST run died with WinError 10048 (16,310 sockets in TIME_WAIT) -- ephemeral-port exhaustion on the CLIENT host, not an engine fault. Rerun with a keep-alive client (engine_lineage.KeepAliveClient); 256/512/1024 then passed. The 32/64/128 rows come from the interrupted run (invariants audited from DB after the fact).
single host: client threads and engine share one machine; latency at 512/1024 includes client-side GIL contention, so the 1024 limit is an upper bound on engine-side queueing
no live-instance bursts: Amendment 4 corroboration on the live engine requires an announced Daedalus window; not run
five_verdict_isolation: answers Q6 only; says nothing about crossing correctness (ED-001..003 live in D16C_CROSSING_QUALIFICATION.json)
